- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; apply upward bias correction by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 20–50% for next 7–14 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model tends to hold or overestimate; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day until reversion stabilizes.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >1.5% daily), consider lagging effect — shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% per day for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1–2 bullish, 1–2 bearish), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model, check if sentiment was neutral or negative 3–5 days prior — if so, model likely missed event-driven volatility; adjust for event-specific shocks.
